<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Mathmitch7" />{{x-larger|{{rh|Lots houſe beſet.|Geneſis|Sodome burnt.}}}} {{rule}}<!-- useful info for KJV Common characters: ſ ¶ ⁊ ⸗ {{sup|†}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Note text''}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Note text}} ‖{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=‖ ''Note text''}}  Remember that v and u are combined, "v" appears at beginnings of words and "u" in the middle Remember that i and j are combined, use "i" or "I" in all cases.--></noinclude>a feaſt, and did bake vnleauened bread, and they did eate.

{{verse|19|4}} ¶ But before they lay downe, the men of the citie, {{smaller|euen}} the men of Sodom, compaſſed the houſe round, both old and yong, all the people from euery quarter.

{{verse|19|5}} And they called vnto Lot, and ſaid vnto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out vnto vs, that we may know them.

{{verse|19|6}} And Lot went out at the doore vnto them, ⁊ ſhut the doore after him,

{{verse|19|7}} And ſaid, I pray you, brethren, doe not ſo wickedly.

{{verse|19|8}} Behold now, I have two daughters, which haue not knowen man; let mee, I pray you, bring them out vnto you, and doe ye to them, as is good in your eyes: onely vnto theſe men do nothing: for therefore came they vnder the ſhadow of my roofe.

{{verse|19|9}} And they ſaid, Stand backe. And they ſaid againe, This one {{smaller|fellow}} came in to ſoiourne, and he will needs be a Iudge: Now wil we deale worſe with thee, then with them. And they preſſed ſore vpon the man, {{smaller|euen}} Lot, and came neere to breake the doore.

{{verse|19|10}} But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the houſe to them, and ſhut the doore.

{{verse|19|11}} And they ſmote the men *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Wiſd.19.16}} that {{smaller|were}} at the doore of the houſe, with blindnes, both ſmall and great: ſo that they wearied themſelues to finde the doore.

{{verse|19|12}} ¶ And the men ſaid vnto Lot, Haſt thou here any beſides? ſonne in law, and thy ſonnes, and thy daughters, and whatſoeuer thou haſt in the citie, bring {{smaller|them}} out of this place.

{{verse|19|13}} For we will deſtroy this place, becauſe the *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chap. 18. 20}} crie of them is waxen great before the face of the LORD: and the LORD hath ſent vs to deſtroy it.

{{verse|19|14}} And Lot went out, and ſpake vnto his ſonnes in law, which married his daughters, and ſaid, Vp, get yee out of this place: for the LORD wil deſtroy this citie: but hee ſeemed as one that mocked, vnto his ſonnes in law.

{{verse|19|15}} ¶ And when the morning aroſe, then the Angels haſtened Lot, ſaying, Ariſe, take thy wife, ⁊ thy two daughters, which {{sup|†}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. are found.''}} are here, leſt thou be conſumed in the ‖{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=‖ ''Or, puniſhment.''}} iniquitie of the citie.

{{verse|19|16}} And *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Wiſd. 10. 6.}} while he lingred, the men laid hold vpon his hand, and vpon the hand of his wife, and vpon the hand of his two daughters, the LORD being mercifull vnto him: and they brought him forth, and ſet him without the citie.

{{verse|19|17}} ¶ And it came to paſſe, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he ſaid, Eſcape for thy life, looke not behind thee, neither ſtay thou in all the plaine: eſcape to the mountaine, leſt thou bee conſumed.

{{verse|19|18}} And Lot ſaid vnto them, Oh not ſo, my Lord.

{{verse|19|19}} Beholde now, thy ſeruant hath found grace in thy ſight, and thou haſt magnified thy mercy, which thou haſt ſhewed vnto me, in ſauing my life, and I cannot eſcape to the mountaine, leſt ſome euill take me, and I die.

{{verse|19|20}} Behold now, this citie is neere to flee vnto, and it is a litle one: Oh let me eſcape thither, (is it not a litle one?) and my ſoule ſhall liue.

{{verse|19|21}} And he ſaid vnto him, See, I haue accepted {{sup|†}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. thy face.''}} thee concerning this thing, that I will not ouerthrow this citie, for the which thou haſt ſpoken.

{{verse|19|22}} Haſte thee, eſcape thither: for I cannot doe any thing till thou bee come thither: therefore the name of the citie was called Zoar.

{{verse|19|23}} ¶ The ſunne was {{sup|†}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. gone forth.''}} riſen vpon the earth, when Lot entred into Zoar.

{{verse|19|24}} Then *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Deut. 29. 23. luk. 17. 29. iſa. 13. 19. ier. 50. 40. amos 4. 11. iude 7.}} the LORD rained vpon Sodome ⁊ vpon Gomorrah, brimſtone and fire, from the LORD out of heauen.

{{verse|19|25}} And he ouerthrew thoſe cities, and all the plaine, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew vpon the ground.

{{verse|19|26}} ¶ But his wife looked backe from behind him, and ſhe became a pillar of ſalt.

{{verse|19|27}} ¶ And Abraham gate vp earely in the morning, to the place, where hee ſtood before the LORD.

{{verse|19|28}} And he looked toward Sodome and Gomorrah, ⁊ toward all the land of the plaine, and beheld, and loe, the ſmoke of the countrey went vp as the ſmoke of a furnace.

{{verse|19|29}} ¶ And it came to paſſe, when God deſtroyed the cities of the plaine, that God remembred Abraham, and ſent Lot out of the midſt of the ouerthrow, when he ouerthrew the cities, in the which Lot dwelt.

{{verse|19|30}} ¶ And Lot went vp out of Zoar, and dwelt in the mountaine, and his<noinclude>{{rh|||two}}</noinclude>
